title: Participial Attributes
summary: Using present and past participles as expanded adjective attributes.
whyItMatters: Participial attributes condense relative clauses and are common in academic, technical, and journalistic writing.

mentalModel.title: Partizip I is active and ongoing
mentalModel.content: The noun performs the action: ein lernendes System.

mentalModel.title: Partizip II is completed or passive
mentalModel.content: The noun has undergone the action: ein trainiertes Modell.

ruleBlocks.title: Form Partizip I with -d
ruleBlocks.content: Add -d to the infinitive and apply normal adjective endings.

ruleBlocks.title: Use Partizip II as an attribute
ruleBlocks.content: Apply adjective endings according to article, gender, case, and number.

ruleBlocks.title: Place expansions before the participle
ruleBlocks.content: Keep the whole attribute before the noun and avoid overload.

examples.de: Die automatisch erzeugten Texte müssen überprüft werden.
examples.en: The automatically generated texts must be checked.

examples.de: Schnell wachsende Datenmengen erhöhen den Rechenaufwand.
examples.en: Rapidly growing data volumes increase computing effort.

examples.de: Die in mehreren Studien bestätigte Wirkung gilt nur für bestimmte Gruppen.
examples.en: The effect confirmed in several studies applies only to certain groups.

commonMistakes.reason: Partizip I adds -d and an adjective ending.

commonMistakes.wrong: Create an attribute too long to parse.
commonMistakes.correct: Use a relative clause when the expansion becomes heavy.

comparisons.summary: Technical descriptions provide authentic active and passive participial attributes.
Clear explanations often unpack dense attributes into relative clauses.
